$comment: Default session layout, modeled on the `mux` function in ~/.functions.
Each tab gets a BSP tree handed to the herdr `layout.apply` socket method.
pane   -> { "label": name, "run": shell command (optional),
"requires_repo": run inside a checkout, see default_repo,
"oneshot": the command prints and exits, see below }
split  -> { "direction": "right"|"down", "ratio": 0-1, "first": node, "second": node }
`run` commands are wrapped so the pane drops back to an interactive shell
when the program exits, instead of the tab going dead.
`{plugin_root}` in a `run` string expands to this directory.
Panes with no `run` are plain shells rooted at the space cwd.
`requires_repo` panes use the space cwd when it is a checkout, and fall back
to default_repo when it is not (a space rooted at ~, say).
An `oneshot` pane prints something and hands the pane straight back, so it
is a banner rather than a program: it does not make its tab worth rebuilding
on restore, and rehydrate types the command into the restored shell instead.
A tab marked `primary_only` is skipped in every space but the primary one,
so global monitors exist once instead of once per project. `secondary_only`
is the mirror: skipped in the primary space, since the repo-oriented TUIs
have no repo to point at from ~. An explicit `apply` builds the whole set.
The same two flags on a *pane* scope its `run` rather than the pane itself:
the pane is still there in every space, just as a plain shell.
`rehydrate_on_startup` relaunches programs tab by tab wherever a restore
brought panes back as bare shells, leaving tabs that hold an agent or a
running program alone. Set it false to only build fresh sessions.
